READ THE LOG↓
LOG 01 / ORDERS RECEIVEDMISSION ACCEPTED

Eight objects. One order. No room to guess.

The arena is taped out and quiet. Somewhere inside it are eight objects — cylinders, cones, boxes, marked blue and pink — and Orion has one job: find them in exact numbered order, confirm what each one actually is, and bring back proof. Not a sweep. Not "whatever's closest." Object one, then two, then three, all the way to eight, no shortcuts.

There's no lidar on board. No depth camera. Orion has a single camera and its own measured sense of where it's been — and that's the whole point. Every step from here is earned by measurement, never assumed.

ORION — SYSTEM LOG
"Sequence loaded: 8 targets, tags 0 through 7. No blind moves permitted. Heading will be derived from what I actually measure, not from what I expect to be true."

LOG 02 / THE HUNTIN PROGRESS

Drive. Stop. Look twice. Move on.

At each waypoint, Orion doesn't just glance and go. It waits for a clean shot — properly framed, not some blurry edge-of-frame guess — before it trusts what it's looking at. Then it runs the object through two independent checks: does the shape and appearance match a registered target, and does the number printed on it agree with that match? If those two signals disagree, that's not swept under the rug — it gets flagged for a human to look at later.

Only once it's confident does Orion do the one thing that actually matters for the mission: it takes the photo, logs exactly where that object sits relative to the nearest waypoint it knows, and moves to the next number in sequence.

ORION — SYSTEM LOG
"Target 03 confirmed. Appearance match agrees with the printed marker. Photo captured, location logged. Proceeding to target 04."

LOG 03 / RETURN WITH EVIDENCESURVEY COMPLETE

The hunt isn't over until the proof is in.

Object eight, confirmed. Orion's sequence is complete — and now every photo it captured, every OCR read, every location it logged travels back with it, not as a claim, but as evidence waiting on a verdict. Nothing Orion found is treated as true yet. It's a field report, not a conclusion.

That report lands in a shared proof gallery — real captured photos, side by side with what the mission log says should be there — for the one part of this system no camera can do on its own: deciding if it's actually right.

LOG 04 / DEBRIEFAWAITING VOTE

What does object two actually mean?

Here's the real question the whole mission is built around: Orion found a cone, marked 02. Its own systems are confident about the shape, the color, the printed number. But out there in the twin world — the shared digital environment everyone's watching — what does "cone, object 02" actually correspond to? A tree? A marker post? Something else entirely?

Orion doesn't get to decide that alone. A human watching the live feed and the twin side by side does — that's the entire reason this mission exists in the first place.

ORION CAPTURED
▲ Object 02
Cone · Pink marker · OCR: "02"
⇄
TWIN CLAIMS
🌲 "Tree"
Digital twin environment
◉ VOTER CONFIRMS MATCH → logged to confirmed_objects["object-02"]

Only once enough voters agree does that answer become permanent — a real lookup anyone can check later: "where is object two?" answered instantly, because a human already settled it.

LOG 05 / OVERWATCHOUTER UGVs ACTIVE

Somewhere else, other eyes are watching.

While Orion works through its sequence, it isn't the only unit in play. Outer UGVs — other real robots, in their own spaces, nowhere near the taped arena — are running their own quiet task in parallel. They're not hunting objects. They don't care about cones or boxes or printed numbers. They have exactly one job: watch for anyone who shouldn't be there.

No votes, no waiting for consensus. The instant an outer unit's camera catches an unregistered person in frame, it doesn't ask permission — it reports immediately: where it saw them, how far that is from the nearest known waypoint, and how that position relates to wherever Orion currently stands.

ALERT SOURCEOuter Unit — Overwatch
DETECTIONUnregistered person, confidence 0.81
DISTANCE TO INNER MISSION≈ 4.2m from Orion's last known position
BROADCASTImmediate — no cooldown gate, no vote required

That alert reaches Orion directly, and now it's Orion's call — not a script's, not an outer unit's:

◍ HOLD POSITION

If whoever was spotted is far enough away, or briefly passing through, Orion can simply hold — finish its current object, stay out of the way, and let the moment pass without breaking sequence.

◍ ABORT MISSION

If the position is close and the risk is real, Orion abandons the sequence entirely — the survey was never worth more than the reason overwatch exists in the first place.

OUTER UNIT — SYSTEM LOG
"Unregistered presence detected, 4.2m from inner mission's last position. Broadcasting now — this doesn't wait for a vote."

FIELDWORK
ORION · THE OUTRIDER

End of log.

No part of this mission counts as true until a person says so — that's not a limitation Orion works around, it's the entire design. Real hardware, real vision, real people making the actual call.
